steps.conclusion: The sound cues for え and け use the vowel in US English “bed” (/ɛ/) without explaining that Japanese /e/ is a little higher. Calling that vowel “pure” does not correct the difference. These cues can teach the wrong vowel despite the correct IPA.

The intro overgeneralizes Japanese writing as left to right in modern text; it should say that this lesson reads left to right, since vertical writing remains common. For う and く, “lips spread” is less accurate than describing relaxed, lightly compressed lips without English-style rounding. “Softening the k” is also less precise than the earlier instruction about reducing the puff of air.
Add one brief reading example using only the taught characters, such as いえ (ie, house), so learners can immediately apply the otherwise well-chosen vowel-and-K sequence.
